signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + BoJ Tightening Repricing
signals.text: The G10 currency scorecard shows JPY leading the G10 complex with a 1W average gain of +1.596% across 7 pairs, while SEK anchors the table at -1.471% across 2 pairs, generating a wide 3.067% bilateral spread. JPY strength is surging as market pricing embeds a BoJ policy rate hike to 1.25% at the upcoming meeting, overriding standard carry headwinds against the Swedish Riksbank's 1.75% policy rate. The macro backdrop is reinforced by economic surprise divergence, with Japan's ESI running strong at +23.8 against Sweden's -6.7. Intraday cross-asset tone remains heavy with Nikkei down -1.93%, supporting JPY outperformance across non-USD crosses. The widening bilateral performance gap reflects fundamental policy divergence as the BoJ tightens into resilient domestic indicators. Trade bias: Bullish JPY against European laggards; policy divergence sustains performance gap. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — market pricing rate hike to 1.25%. Risk: BoJ leaves policy rate unchanged at 1.00%, prompting sharp unwind of front-loaded JPY gains.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Spec Long vs Extreme Retail Short Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7177, consolidating just below its daily SMA20 at 0.7164 while holding well above its SMA50 at 0.7065 and SMA200 at 0.7001. CFTC positioning reveals leveraged funds hold a crowded net long of +50,250 contracts (94th percentile, z +1.79), pointing to stretched institutional exposure. In contrast, retail positioning via Myfxbook displays an extreme 91% short imbalance, establishing a direct structural divergence against institutional positioning. Cash policy rates currently favor AUD with RBA at 4.35% vs Fed at 3.75% delivering a 60bp carry advantage, backed by an AONIA-SOFR spread of 71bp. However, the options market remains cautious with a mild 1-month 25-delta risk reversal put skew of -0.55 and a +1.3% vol risk premium (IV 7.0% vs HV30 5.7%). Stretched positioning leaves the pair highly sensitive to US yield curve moves ahead of critical inflation releases. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; retail short capitulation supports upside continuation. Catalyst: US CPI at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Leveraged funds liquidate crowded longs on a US yield surge, pushing price below the SMA50 at 0.7065.
evidence: RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75% — 60bp AUD carry premium

signals.title: EUR/USD — ECB Tightening Stance vs Impending US CPI Volatility
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1598, pinned below its daily SMA20 at 1.1629 and SMA200 at 1.1637, but holding above its SMA50 at 1.1529. The ECB delivered a 25bp rate increase to 2.50%, reinforcing an active hiking cycle path into year-end, while the Fed remains on hold at 3.75%. The policy rate differential of Fed 3.75% vs ECB 2.5% maintains a 1 in favor of USD (SOFR vs €STR at +145bp), containing broader EUR upside momentum. Leveraged funds hold a net short of -52,784 contracts (31st percentile, z -0.39), while asset managers sit heavily long (+291,129 contracts), establishing balanced institutional positioning. Options markets price elevated short-term risk with IV at 5.0% against HV30 at 4.1% (+0.9% VRP), as the US yield curve bear-steepens with 2s10s at +51.4bp. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD; macro carry advantage offsets hawkish ECB policy guidance. Catalyst: US CPI at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US core inflation prints above 0.3% m/m, reinforcing Fed hike probabilities and breaking technical support below 1.1529.
